text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT TENDERS - Pakistan will be holding side-by-side tenders for 315,000 tonnes of Australian white milling wheat and U.S. soft white wheat. Bids will be opened on January 12 and must be valid until the following day. Shipment was slated for February 1-28.

WHEAT TENDERS - Sri Lanka's state buying arm, the Co-operative Wholesale Establishment seeks 100,000 tonnes of soft and hard wheat, government officials said. The tender closes January 3 and is for 50,000 of soft wheat for delivery in the third week of January and 50,000 tonnes of hard wheat for delivery in the second week of February.

- The Commodity Credit Corp (CCC) of the U.S. Agriculture Department said it seeks up to 30,000 tonnes of U.S. No. 2 or better hard red winter wheat for donation to Bosnia. Shipment is for January 25-February 20. Offers are due January 7.

WHEAT TENDERS - Yemen on January 7 will seek 200,000 tonnes of optional soft wheat flour for shipment between February and June and 200,000 tonnes of new-crop U.S. or Canadian or Australian soft white wheat for July-September, European traders said.

- Bangladesh seeks 100,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 wheat or Australian Standard or better Canadian winter red/spring wheat for shipment by February 21, food ministry officials said. Offers are to be opened January 18 and the results announced two to three days later.

BARLEY TENDER - Saudi Arabia was expected to tender next week for barley, Canadian grain sources said on Thursday. European traders said last week they expected Saudi Arabia to seek about 500,000 tonnes of barley this week.

SOYBEAN OIL TENDER - The CCC is to tender for 10,370 tonnes of U.S. bulk crude degummed soybean oil for donation to Peru. Delivery will be February 3-18. Offers were requested by January 7. Successful offerers will be notified January 8.

MARKET TALK - A Chinese newspaper on Thursday forecast a stable domestic wheat market in 1997 and said falling world prices would create a favorable environment for wheat imports. International wheat prices were expected to drop in 1997, the Economic Information Daily said.

MARKET TALK - Talk was widespread in U.S. grain markets on Thursday that Egypt may tender for 400,000 to 500,000 tonnes of optional origin wheat as early as next week for February/March shipment, U.S. exporters said. Several exporters said they could not confirm the Egyptian tender but they did not rule out the possibility.
